( First Revision )
0. FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 29 February 1980, after the draft finalized by the Fertilizers Sectional Committee had been approved by the Petroleum, Coal and Related Products Division Council. 0.2 While potassium chloride is the most used source of potassic fertilizer, certain specialized crops like tobacco need chloride-free potassic fertilizers like the sulphate, as these are sensitive to chlorides. 0.3 This standard was first published in 1964. This revision has been undertaken to include the requirement for particle size of the material as Further, since separate standards it is important for the trade and users. on methods of sampling and test for fertilizers have been published those details have, therefore, been deleted from this standard. 0.4 In the preparation of this standard, consideration has been given to the need for maintaining co-ordination with the specification of the Fertilizer ( Control ) Order, 1957 and the Essential Commodities Act, However this standard is subject to the 1955 of Government of India. provisions imposed under this Order wherever applicable. 0.5 For particle size, the use of IS sieves conforming to IS : 460-1962* prescribed. Where IS sieves are not available, other standard sieves judged from aperture size may be used. is as

0.6 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with The number of significant places retained in the rounded IS : 2-19601_. off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1.1This standard prescribes the requirements and the methods of sampling and test for potassium sulphate, fertilizer grade.

NOTE- The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is goverued by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act and the Rules and Regulatious made therevnder. The IS1 Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operatec by the producer, IS1 marked produbts are also continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of condition under wh;ch a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufactureas or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institutions. 4.2 Criteria for Conformity - For declaring the conformity of the lot to the requirements of this specification, the test results on the composite sample shall satisfy all the requirements specified in 2. 5.
